diagnosis.rootCause: The water only ever reflects the sky. The realtime reflection probe that feeds gi.indirect.specular in LightingWater has cullingMask 0 (ZoneBuilder.Awake). So ponds and creeks never mirror the banks, trees, houses, bridges, the mill wheel or the player; they show the same smooth sky gradient everywhere, broken up only by the ripple normal map. A few things hide the problem instead of fixing it: the 45% "below the horizon" fade in LightingWater, the flattened ripples at grazing angles, and the capped glare. That missing mirror of the surroundings, with no dark reflected tree lines and no contact reflection at the banks, is the main reason the water reads as plastic.
diagnosis.approach:
Options considered (built-in pipeline, gamma space, HDR camera, water at Transparent-10 after a GrabPass):
(a) A planar reflection camera. Chosen. It is the only option that shows correct, parallax-true reflections of things that are off-screen or hidden, like tree tops above the frame, the far bank and bridge undersides. That is what a third-person camera looking down at water mostly sees. Cost is one extra render at reduced resolution, and only while water is on screen.
(b) SSR from the GrabPass plus _CameraDepthTexture. Rejected. It needs about 32-64 depth taps plus refinement per full-res water pixel. It can only reflect what is already on screen, so looking down at a creek loses the sky and tree tops above the frame. It also breaks up at silhouettes and screen edges, so it would fall back to the probe most of the time. Similar or higher cost than (a) for a worse picture.
(c) A probe that also sees scenery, time-sliced. Rejected as the main fix. A single cubemap has no parallax: a pond 20 m from the probe centre shows houses in the wrong place and at the wrong size. It also costs 6 renders plus convolution and lags. The existing sky probe stays as the fallback wherever the planar reflection has no answer.

What I implemented (new component Scripts/World/WaterReflection.cs, added by ZoneBuilder.BuildWater):
- Once per frame, from Camera.onPreCull of the main camera (so it matches the final camera exactly, including capture renders), it mirrors about ONE water level. The level comes from the visible water nearest the camera: frustum-tested renderer bounds, a lake's flat level, or a creek's level at the point nearest the camera via ZoneWater.Project. Hysteresis keeps the choice from flipping between two nearby bodies.
- Nothing is rendered when no water is in view, when the nearest water is more than 120 m away, or when the camera is at or under the plane.
- The mirror camera uses the classic setup: mirrored worldToCameraMatrix, an oblique near plane 5 cm above the water (so beds, underwater banks, wading legs and the wheel's lower paddles are clipped), a culling matrix from the non-oblique projection, and GL.invertCulling.
- It renders at half the camera's resolution (width capped at 1024) into an HDR mipmapped RenderTexture. During that render it turns off shadows (shadowDistance 0, so no second shadow map), fog, MSAA and occlusion culling, and allows at most 2 pixel lights. Everything is restored in a finally block before the main camera culls.
- The reflection leaves out the water (surfaces now go on Unity's built-in Water layer, 4), grass and particles. Grass is drawn with DrawMeshInstanced on layer 1 (TransparentFX). Leaves, ash, splashes and ripple rings, Wasting motes and chimney smoke are set to layer 1 too. That also avoids soft particles reading a stale depth texture.
- It is re-created only when the size changes, so there are no per-frame allocations.
- Globals: _WaterReflection, _WaterReflectionDepth (the depth sub-element), _WaterReflectionInvProj (inverse GPU oblique projection) and _WaterReflectionParams = (level, live, RenderSettings.reflectionIntensity, bend). Every other camera (zone map, scene view, probes) gets live = 0 and keeps using the sky probe. There is also a static Enabled switch for a future graphics option.

Shader changes, in three delimited PLANAR REFLECTION regions of Water.shader. The Properties block, Input struct, surf body and k/glare lines are untouched.
1. After the include: globals, two statics, and the helpers WaterScreen, WaterMirrorDepth, WaterFogFactor and WaterPlanar.
   - Lookup: take the reflected ray from the world-space ripple normal and blend it toward a flat mirror by bend (0.25, because full-strength ripples shatter a mirror). March it to the reflected thing's distance, estimated from the reflection's depth (sky counts as 50 m). Project that point with the main camera's VP, using the same ComputeScreenPos convention as screenPos, and sample the mip-blurred reflection by roughness.
   - Water at another level than the mirror: the lookup is shifted by twice the level difference. The reflection fades to the sky probe between 0.5 and 1.3 m of difference, and when the bent lookup leaves the screen.
   - Fog: the reflection is rendered without fog, and the shader adds back fog for the reflected leg only. It uses clarity(total path) / clarity(eye to water), because the surface's own fog already covers eye to water. This keeps hazy Khaven trees hazy in their reflection. The oblique projection would otherwise have removed fog from the reflection entirely, because Unity's fog coordinate comes from clip z.
2. In LightingWater, base pass only (the add pass must not add the reflection twice): gi.indirect.specular = lerp(probe, planar, alpha), and r.y is lifted by alpha. The existing k line then drops its 45% below-horizon fade, which was a stand-in for missing banks, only where real banks are shown. All the existing fresnel/_Reflect/_Glare shaping still applies to the planar reflection.
3. At the end of surf: hand IN.screenPos and IN.worldPos to the lighting function through the statics (same pixel, same pass).

Night and zone murk:
- The planar reflection is multiplied by RenderSettings.reflectionIntensity, which WorldClock dims to 0.55 at night, the same as the probe. It then goes through k (_Reflect) and is capped by _Glare, and the night scene itself is dark. So night water stays dark, with only lamp and window streaks capped at _Glare.
- Khaven's murky material (_Reflect 0.3, lower _Glare, high _Murk) scales the reflection the same way, and the see-through murk and foam are unchanged. So it stays murky.
- Levels, meshes and water queries are untouched (WaterTests invariants hold). Water surfaces only change layer.

Also added a PlayMode test (WaterReflectionTests) checking the wiring: every Crulanda/Water surface is registered and on the Water layer, and every zone particle system is on the no-reflect layer.

Rendering the reflection camera inside Camera.onPreCull of the main camera is a nested render. This is standard in the built-in pipeline (the classic water script renders from OnWillRenderObject) but unverified in this Unity 6000.6 project. If it errors, move the Pick+Draw call into a LateUpdate with [DefaultExecutionOrder(10000)] and keep onPreCull only for turning the params on and off per camera.

The shader passes data from surf to LightingWater through static globals (wrScreenPos, wrWorldPos). Valid HLSL/HLSLcc and used in practice, but it depends on surface-shader codegen calling surf before the lighting function in the same fragment, which it does for ForwardBase.

Fog restoration relies on Shader.SetGlobalTexture(id, rt, RenderTextureSubElement.Depth) giving a sampleable depth on D3D11. If the binding fails, reflections lose their extra haze (unfogged far trees in Khaven), and in the worst case look fog-coloured. Check the Frame Debugger for _WaterReflectionDepth. As a fallback, make WaterMirrorDepth return -1, which disables the extra fog and the depth-based bend distance.

One mirror level per frame: water more than about 1.3 m above or below the chosen level falls back to the sky probe (faded from 0.5 m). A steep creek seen far along its length therefore goes back to sky reflection in the distance, and the reflection can pop when the nearest body changes to one at a different level.

Cost: roughly doubles draw calls and culling while water is on screen, at half resolution, with no shadows, fog or MSAA and at most 2 pixel lights. The reflection is unshadowed, so reflected ground under trees is slightly brighter than the real ground. Tunables: scale, maxWidth, maxDistance, and WaterReflection.Enabled (a static off switch).

Changing layers: water surfaces move to built-in layer 4 (Water). Grass, splash and ring particles, leaves, ash, motes and chimney smoke move to layer 1 (TransparentFX). The main camera renders Everything, and nothing uses layer masks except SphereCastAll(~0) and DefaultRaycastLayers. Water and particles have no colliders, so gameplay is unaffected.
bend = 0.25 assumes the current ripple strength. If the other agent makes ripples stronger or weaker, retune bend (it's a component field, not a material property).

Shader:
- The PLANAR REFLECTION block sits after the include and before LightingWater, so nothing is used before it is declared.
- The statics are written in surf and read in LightingWater. Both run in the same frag_surf, and surf runs before the GI and lighting calls.
- The surface-shader generator defines UNITY_PASS_FORWARDBASE before the user snippet, and the add pass has no indirect specular, so gating on it is correct.
- IN.screenPos and IN.worldPos are already Input members, so there are no new interpolators.
- Sampler count after the change is about 5 user plus the built-in ones, well under 16.
- These are all available in the fragment stage from UnityCG and UnityShaderVariables:
  - tex2Dlod
  - ComputeScreenPos
  - UNITY_MATRIX_VP
  - unity_FogColor, unity_FogParams
  - UNITY_CALC_FOG_FACTOR_RAW
  - unity_OrthoParams
- The multi_compile_fog variants define FOG_* in the passes that matter.
- `return 0` from a half4 function is a legal scalar promotion.
- No name clashes were found.
- Off-screen or behind-camera lookups cannot produce NaN: live drops to 0, and uv is only clamped.

Maths:
- Mirror, oblique plane and mirrored transform: flip (m11 = -1, m13 = 2L) with view = W*flip, the oblique plane from view.MultiplyPoint((0, L+offset, 0)) and view.MultiplyVector(up), and Euler(-x, y, z). This is exactly the Standard Assets Water / MirrorReflection construction. Worked through by hand, the kept half-space is real geometry with y > L + offset.
- cullingMatrix = P * view: correct plane extraction even though the view matrix is mirrored, and it avoids culling by the skewed oblique far plane.
- UV orientation: the mirror renders into a render texture without MSAA or image effects, so Unity stores it in GL orientation. ComputeScreenPos (with its _ProjectionParams.x fix) gives view-oriented uvs whether or not the main camera's HDR/OnRenderImage target is flipped. No _TexelSize flip is needed for this texture.
- GL.GetGPUProjectionMatrix(proj, false).inverse is the right inverse for (uv*2-1, raw depth), because the stored depth is in GL y orientation and platform z (reversed on D3D).
- The level shift (lookup at R'(p) - lift, with lift = 2(w.y - L)) is correct.
- Fog: re-applying fog with the ratio F(d)/F(eye) reproduces fog over the full path, F(d)*c + (1 - F(d))*fog, for the reflected term.
- Night and murk: the reflection goes through reflectionIntensity (0.55 at night), then k/_Reflect, the Fresnel term, and both _Glare caps. Night water stays dark, and Khaven's lower _Reflect keeps it murky.

Layers are safe:
- The main camera's mask in Oakhaven.unity is Everything, and TagManager has 1 = TransparentFX and 4 = Water.
- Nothing uses layer masks beyond SphereCastAll(~0) and DefaultRaycastLayers, and water and particles have no colliders.
- NavMesh sources are explicit meshes, boxes and modifiers, not layers.
- No prefab or scene contains a ParticleSystem, so the test's claim that every zone particle system is on layer 1 holds. The four particle creators are exactly the ones patched.
- Only the Crulanda/Water surfaces go to layer 4. The troughs and well that use art.water (Standard) keep layer 0.

Nested render: calling Render() on a different camera from inside the main camera's pre-cull has established built-in precedent. Examples are Standard Assets Water (OnWillRenderObject) and camera-OnPreCull portal renderers. The proposal's LateUpdate fallback is a sensible plan B.

diagnosis.rootCause:
Why the water looks like plastic (from Water.shader, ZoneSceneBuilder.NormalTex and the screenshots):
1) Only one regular ripple texture. NormalTex adds 7 sine waves of 0.9-3 m wavelength and multiplies the slopes by 18, which gives an RMS slope of about 2.2. The normals are therefore saturated near 60 degrees, with hard creases. The shader samples this texture twice at almost the same scale (uv*0.11 and x1.9), multiplies by _Bump 0.3 and gets a surface RMS slope of about 0.34, roughly 3x real water in a light breeze. On the pond and the creek this shows as big, regular, rounded blobs of sky and bed ('jelly' or 'tar' in oakhaven-99-pond, 17-brook-pond, 06-mill and khaven-99-creek).
2) The highlights are broad. _Gloss 0.82 times further reductions gives GGX roughness of about 0.03 or more. On large smooth ripples that is a wide sheen, and _Glare then clamps it flat. There is no fine facet structure to break the sun into glitter.
3) The ripples slide rather than flow. Both layers move rigidly at one speed, the same mid-channel as at the banks, and are not stretched along the current. It reads as a scrolling texture.
4) The vertex swell is two sines aligned to the x and z axes, at about half the real speed of shallow-water waves, so the surface looks like it is breathing.
5) The see-through has one colour. The bed under the water is the same colour and brightness as the dry bank, and absorption is the same for every channel, so the surface looks like a clear pane laid over the ground. There is no wet edge and no red-first depth shift.
(The sky-only reflection probe is the other cluster and is left to the reflections agent.)
diagnosis.approach:
Seven separate, clearly marked ('---- WATER DETAIL: ... (begin/end) ----') regions in Water.shader, with no rewrite of the whole file. The ripple block keeps the names 'slope', 'uv', 'flowing', 'd1' and 'dist' that other code uses. LightingWater, Behind(), the Input struct and the declaration line are not touched, so the reflections agent can edit them.
- Ripples: a new broadband wavelet normal map (_Wavelets) generated by WaveletTex in ZoneSceneBuilder. It has 56 sine wavelets in random directions with log-spaced wavelengths of 2-30 cm per tile, exact whole periods so it tiles seamlessly, amplitude proportional to k^-1.2, and slopes scaled to RMS 0.4 with a fixed seed. It is sampled as two octaves rotated against each other: tiles of 2.2 m and 0.94 m, turned 37 and 120 degrees, with the slopes rotated back into the tangent frame.
- Flow: creeks use a two-phase flow map. The current is 1.3x _FlowSpeed mid-channel and 0.35x at the banks, using vertex alpha (shallowness), and the ripples are stretched 1/0.6 along the current. Noise staggers the phases and a variance-preserving blend avoids any visible pulse. Lakes drift the two octaves in different directions.
- The old _Normal becomes a faint long swell at 0.3 weight, and its generator gain drops from x18 to x6, so it is a smooth height field instead of saturated blobs. Creeks are 1.1x as rough and ponds 0.75x, giving RMS slope of about 0.10-0.15.
- Highlights: daylight _Gloss goes up to 0.95, with specular anti-aliasing (Tokuyoshi-Kaplanyan) from ddx/ddy of the normal, capped at 0.1, plus a small roughness term that grows with distance. The old ad-hoc slope and distance factors are replaced. By moonlight the gloss eases back to the old 0.82 through the light's brightness (lightK), so night highlights are no brighter than today.
- Sparkle: a separate emissive glint term. It is a tight lobe (exponent _GlintSharp 900) on the uncalmed ripple normal, so it also works at grazing sun angles, and it is allowed above the _Glare cap so it sparkles through the bloom (Karis-filtered). It widens and dims with the pixel footprint (fwidth), fades out between 25 and 70 m, and is scaled by the light colour times lightK (moon glints are about 0.1 HDR, so night stays dark) and by saturate(_Glare). It is zero under foam and on the ortho map. The sun direction in tangent space is computed in vert and carried in the vertex colour rgb. The water meshes leave that channel white and surf never read it, and alpha (shallowness) is kept. This avoids adding INTERNAL_DATA to Input, which the other agent might also touch.
- Colour: per-channel absorption (_Absorb 1.3/1/0.75 times _Murk, so red goes first; the average murk is unchanged, so Khaven stays murky). The bed seen through water gets a wet look, darker at 0.8 and 1.2x saturation, ramping in over the first 6 cm of water. This gives the slight darkening at the waterline.
- Foam streaks: faint lines stretched along the current, mid-channel only, drifting downstream at 1.2x flow and broken into flecks. They are max()-combined into the existing foam (_Streaks 0.22). Lakes, the map and water beyond 60 m get none. The touch-foam is unchanged.
- Swell: three crossing, non-axis-aligned waves at shallow-water speeds (2.2-2.9 rad/s). _Wave drops from 0.025 to 0.012, creeks get 40% of it, and the shore calm is kept.
- ZoneBuilder: murky zones scale _Glint by waterReflect (Khaven x0.3). This also helps the step-1 leftover 'Khaven's creek has hot sun glints near the camera'.
- Cost: 3 extra normal-texture fetches (5 in total), 4 value-noise calls, ddx/fwidth and one pow. There are no new passes, cameras or allocations. The new texture is generated once per validation build (about 0.1-0.2 s).

problems: LIKELY COMPILE FAILURE (silent fallback). The patched surf reads IN.color in three places: IN.color.a in the ripple block, (1 - IN.color.a) in the streaks, and IN.color.rgb in the glints. Today surf never reads IN.color, so surface-shader analysis leaves the COLOR interpolator out. Reading it adds a COLOR0 slot to every pass. At #pragma target 3.0 this shader's ForwardBase already fills about 10 of 10 interpolators: pack0 (uv_Normal), tSpace0-2, screenPos, custompack0 (flowFlag), sh, fog, shadow coords, and the '#if SHADER_TARGET >= 30 float4 lmap' dynamic-lightmap slot. An 11th gives 'Too many texture interpolators would be used for ForwardBase pass'. The shader then errors, and the build silently falls back to Legacy Transparent/Diffuse, which CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md already warns about. The proposal's risk note ('one interpolator is fine on DX11/Vulkan/Metal') is wrong: the surface-shader generator enforces the limit set by #pragma target on every platform.

FIX for the above, at no interpolator cost. (a) The shallowness (vertex alpha) goes to surf in flowFlag.y: vert sets o.flowFlag.y = v.color.a. uv2.y is always 0 in ZoneWater.Finish, and nothing reads flowFlag.y. (b) The sun direction is put in tangent space in surf, using 'float3 worldNormal; INTERNAL_DATA' plus WorldNormalVector(IN, axis) to get T, B and N. The pass already carries tSpace because o.Normal is written and viewDir is needed, so this adds no interpolator. The tangent-frame maths and the v.color.rgb write in vert are dropped.

MERGE POINT: the fix has to add 'float3 worldNormal; INTERNAL_DATA' to the Input line, which the proposal meant to leave alone. If the reflections patch also adds INTERNAL_DATA (for example with worldRefl), keep a single INTERNAL_DATA or the two definitions will clash.
Minor: the wet-bed transform also ran on the orthographic zone map, where 'below' is already 'deep', so the map water shifted colour. It is now guarded with unity_OrthoParams.w.

SCOPE (user request wins): Chris only asked to add this to the to-do list. It is already recorded as 'Step 5, water realism pass 2' in Docs/CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md (working copy, not committed). Keep these patches for Step 5 and do not apply them now.

Tuning interaction: the daytime gloss rises from about 0.77 effective to 0.95, so the 64 px sky probe is sampled near mip 0.5 instead of about 2.3. Sky reflections become sharper and may look low-res; check this together with the reflections patch. By moonlight the gloss is about 0.83, slightly glossier than the old effective 0.77. The moon highlight is tighter but still capped by _Glare, and moon glints peak at about 0.09 HDR, below the night bloom threshold of 0.55. Night stays dark.

Checked and OK: every oldString matches exactly once in the current files (applied to scratch copies with the Edit tool). Declarations come before use: _Wavelets, _Absorb and the floats are declared above WaveletSlope, and p, shallow, flowing, dist, fp, foam and rawSlope are all defined before they are used. The HLSL is valid (float2x2 constructors, mul with rot and with R^T for the slope, the lerp promotions, ddx/fwidth outside divergent branches, and the WorldNormalVector macro with float3(...) arguments). The C# compiles: System.IO and UnityEditor are imported, System.Random is fully qualified so it does not clash with UnityEngine.Random, and r is in scope in ZoneBuilder. water_normal.png and Water surface.mat are not in D:, so robocopy /MIR deletes them and BuildOakhaven, called from EncounterBuildPlayer.Build, regenerates them. The x6 gain and the new shader defaults therefore take effect. There are no mesh or level changes, so WaterTests are untouched, and nothing depends on graphicsDeviceType. There are no reflection cameras, oblique planes or render textures in this patch, so those checks do not apply.

review.notes:
Verdict: fixable. The design and maths are sound, but as written the shader would probably fail to compile and fall back without any error in the game.

The problem: the patch reads IN.color (vertex colour) in surf in three places. Today surf never reads it, so it costs nothing. Reading it adds a COLOR interpolator on top of what I estimate is already 10 of 10 at #pragma target 3.0 (ForwardBase: pack0, tSpace0-2, screenPos, custompack0, sh, fog, shadow coords, and the SHADER_TARGET>=30 lmap slot). The likely result is 'Too many texture interpolators', and the water silently falls back to Legacy Transparent/Diffuse. The generator enforces this limit on every platform, so the proposal's 'fine on DX11' does not hold.

The corrected edits move the shallowness into flowFlag.y (set in vert; uv2.y is always 0 and nothing reads it). They get the tangent-space sun from WorldNormalVector through 'float3 worldNormal; INTERNAL_DATA', which uses no interpolator because the tangent frame (tSpace) is already carried. This is the one place that touches the Input line. If the reflections patch also adds INTERNAL_DATA, keep only one.

I applied all 12 corrected edits to scratch copies (C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--code-mmo\be58a4b3-4c77-45ef-9182-17eb205878fc\scratchpad\wd\). Every oldString matched exactly once, and I read the shader end to end for declaration order and syntax. Nothing was compiled; Unity was not run.

Other checks:
- **Night:** moon glints peak at about 0.09 HDR, under the 0.55 night bloom threshold. Gloss by moonlight is about 0.83. The moon highlight stays capped at _Glare.
- **Khaven:** the average murk is unchanged, and glints are scaled by 0.3 × 0.86.
- **Regeneration:** water_normal.png and Water surface.mat are not in D:, so robocopy /MIR deletes them and BuildOakhaven regenerates them. The x6 gain and the new defaults do take effect.
- **Tests and cost:** WaterTests are unaffected (no mesh or level change), and nothing new runs per frame on the CPU.
- **Not applicable:** the reflection-maths checks (oblique clip plane, UV flip, render texture lifetime, culling masks); this patch has no reflection camera.

Add to verify step 2: grep the logs for 'Too many texture interpolators' as well as 'Shader error'. Also check the sky reflections at day gloss 0.95: the 64 px probe is now sampled near mip 0.5 and may look low-res, so tune this together with the reflections patch.

Scope: Chris only asked for this to go on the to-do list, and it already does: 'Step 5, water realism pass 2' in Docs/CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md, uncommitted in the working copy. Keep these patches for Step 5 and do not apply them now. Step 2, zone looks, is next.
